claims.statement: The admin SPA obtains a session only through POST /api/auth/login on the Fastify backend: the route signs in against Supabase Auth with the service-role client and returns just the access token and identity, so the browser holds no Supabase client (ADR-0006).

Every login refusal in POST /api/auth/login is produced by one shared `deny` helper in a fixed order — throttle pre-check, dev-credential gate, GoTrue sign-in, then admin_users membership — so no branch can diverge in response shape.

Every login denial returns the identical 401 UNAUTHORIZED body with message `Invalid email or password` after a uniform `DENIAL_MIN_MS` = 250 ms sleep, deliberately making a throttled attempt, a refused dev credential, a wrong password, and a non-admin sign-in indistinguishable to the client.
The reason a login was denied is written only to structured security-event log lines on the request logger, never to an HTTP response.

The security-event catalog is `security.sign_in_success`, `security.sign_in_failure`, `security.sign_in_throttled`, and `security.sign_out`, each emitted with event, account, source (request.ip) and outcome so lines correlate by reqId with the request audit line.
A malformed login body fails zod validation in the central error handler as 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, before credential verification, so it is never counted as a failed attempt by the throttler.
A successful login returns the GoTrue access token plus `{ id, email, name }`, where name comes from `user_metadata.full_name` (empty string when absent), and the session's refresh token is dropped.

Login throttling is per-process and in-memory (ADR-0005): keys are the normalized account (trimmed lowercased email) and the request IP, five failures inside a five-minute window block a key for fifteen minutes, and an active block outlasts pruning of the underlying failures.
Each failed attempt records a failure against both the account key and the source key, a successful sign-in clears both, and the throttled pre-check refusal records nothing new.
The throttler is instantiated per app instance inside registerAuth, so each buildApp() gets isolated state and a process restart clears every counter and block.
The throttle source key is Fastify's `request.ip` and buildApp never enables `trustProxy`, so behind a reverse proxy per-source throttling would collapse onto the proxy's address.

The dev credential is a hard-coded DEV_CREDENTIAL constant that the login route refuses, before calling GoTrue and through the ordinary denied branch with a failure recorded, whenever ALLOW_DEV_CREDENTIAL is false (its default).
ALLOW_DEV_CREDENTIAL=true does not make the dev pair trusted: the pair still has to sign in through GoTrue and pass the admin_users check.

The dev credential is a committed, dev-only fixture: supabase/seed.sql inserts the admin auth.users row with a bcrypt hash of that password and is executed verbatim by the Supabase CLI with no environment interpolation, so it must be replaced through Supabase Auth before shared use.
ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD are required by the env schema but never read by server code; only the integration-test helpers use them to sign in the seeded admin.

Administrative membership is decided by one shared rule, `isAdminUserId(db, userId)`, which queries the admin_users table; the admin guard, the login route, and GET /api/auth/me all call it instead of doing their own lookup.

The admin guard is a single preHandler registered on the /api/admin plugin before its child modules, parses a strict single-part Bearer header, answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED for a missing or invalid token and 403 FORBIDDEN for a non-admin, and records request.adminUserId which the onResponse audit line logs as adminId.

admin_users membership is read from the database on every request rather than embedded in the token, so granting or revoking administrative access takes effect on the next call with no restart and no token rotation.

GET /api/auth/me repeats the same token verification and admin_users check as the guard and returns `{ id, email, name }`, answering 401 without a token and 403 for a signed-in non-admin; it is registered outside the admin plugin and therefore not itself behind the guard.

The SPA's `restoreSession()` distinguishes three boot outcomes: no stored token short-circuits to unauthenticated without calling /me; a successful /me yields authenticated; a 401 clears the stored token and yields unauthenticated; a transport failure or any 5xx yields unreachable with the token kept, and any other failure signs out while keeping the token.

RequireAuth renders a loading spinner while status is loading, the BackendUnreachable retry plate when status is unreachable, and a redirect to /login carrying returnTo and the sessionExpired flag otherwise; retry re-runs the session restore.

The session token is a plain browser value stored in localStorage under `komyuter.admin.token`, attached by the axios request interceptor as `Authorization: Bearer`, and written only by the login API function.

The axios response interceptor treats any 401 whose URL does not end in /api/auth/login as a mid-use session expiry: it saves the current path to sessionStorage, clears the stored token, and emits on the sessionExpired bus, which AuthProvider converts into the unauthenticated state.

The post-expiry return path is sanitized: `getReturnPath` accepts only strings starting with / and not //, `getSessionExpired` accepts only a literal true, and the login screen prefers the sessionStorage copy of the path over router location state and clears it after use.

There is no token renewal path: the login response omits the refresh token, the admin app has no refresh call, and supabase/config.toml sets jwt_expiry to 3600 seconds, so an expired access token ends the session until a fresh sign-in.

POST /api/auth/logout is idempotent by contract: it best-effort revokes a resolvable token globally, swallows revocation failures, emits exactly one security.sign_out event with the resolved email or "unknown", and always answers 204 with an empty body for a valid, invalid, or missing token.

The admin SPA never calls POST /api/auth/logout: its signOut() only clears the stored token and resets auth state before navigating to /login, so a UI sign-out leaves the GoTrue session valid until the token expires — contradicting the "sign-out → POST /api/auth/logout, global revocation" description in docs/ADMIN.md.

The origin allowlist is a root onRequest hook registered immediately after @fastify/cors, so it covers /api/status and /api/auth/* as well as /api/admin; a present Origin not in ADMIN_ORIGINS is refused with 403 FORBIDDEN, while OPTIONS preflights and requests without an Origin header pass through.

The server integration suite pins the auth contract: unified 401 denial with a measured minimum delay for wrong-password and non-admin cases, account blocking after five failures from distinct sources, source blocking against another account, counter clearing on success, both dev-credential gate states, the origin-guard outcomes including the OPTIONS pass, and 204-plus-revocation for logout, while a separate suite pins the guard's 401/403 behaviour on the /api/admin subtree.

Client-side unit tests pin the session behaviour: the three restoreSession outcomes including the token kept on 403, the 401 interceptor side effects and its login-URL exemption, and return-path sanitization together with the sessionExpired flag parsing.
